narr: Showers and thunderstorms streaming northward well ahead of approaching Hurricane Henri resulted in flash flooding across portions of northeast New Jersey. This rainfall developed in a moisture-rich environment, with the 8pm sounding from Upton, NY recording precipitable water values around 2.25 inches. Rainfall totals from this predecessor rainfall event ranged from 1-4 inches, with the ASOS at Teterboro Airport reporting 2.40 inches and a COOP observer in Harrison reporting 2.91 inches.
ev: The westbound lanes of NJ Route 3 were closed in Clifton due to flooding.
All lanes were closed due to flooding on the I-280 eastbound exit ramp to Northfield Avenue in Orange.
Madison Street in Hoboken was closed due to flash flooding.
All lanes were closed on the northbound US Route 1&9 Truck Route at Charlotte Circle in Jersey City.
Frank E. Rodgers Boulevard was closed south of Bergen Street in Harrison due to flooding. Multiple vehicles were stranded, including a law enforcement vehicle, and water rescues were ongoing.
The southbound lanes of US Routes 1&9 were closed north of Grand Street in Elizabeth due to flooding.
All lanes were closed on NJ Route 17 in Hasbrouck Heights due to flooding.

The Peckman River at Ozone Avenue in Verona quickly rose above minor flood stage (3.5 feet) at 12:35am EDT August 22, crested at a height of 3.78 feet at 12:40am EDT, and fell back below flood stage at 12:55am EDT.
